summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 7.9), verified it detects and clears changes correctly, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol with boot-identity and recovery proof.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 7.9, no aide installed, no yum repos enabled)
Cleared a stale yum lock left by a prior timed-out install attempt
Confirmed outbound HTTPS reachability to vault.centos.org (CentOS7-compatible mirror)
Downloaded aide-0.15.1-13.el7.x86_64.rpm from vault.centos.org and installed it via rpm -ivh
Reviewed /etc/aide.conf: default RHEL7 config already applies a recursive PERMS rule across all of /etc plus CONTENT_EX (SHA256+perms) rules for dozens of critical /etc subpaths/files
Ran 'aide --init' to build the initial database, then copied aide.db.new.gz to aide.db.gz to activate it as the baseline
Ran 'aide --check' confirming a clean baseline ('All files match AIDE database')

Appended a line to /etc/issue (a tracked file) and re-ran 'aide --check', confirming AIDE detected the SHA256 change (exit code 4, 1 changed file) - proving the baseline can identify later /etc changes
Reverted the /etc/issue change and re-ran 'aide --check' to confirm baseline returned to clean
Captured pre-restart boot_id, uptime -s, and aide.db.gz md5sum as the healthy baseline
Issued 'shutdown -r now' via nohup/background so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until SSH connectivity returned
Captured post-restart boot_id (changed) and uptime -s (new boot time) as proof of an actual restart
Re-verified aide.db.gz md5sum unchanged and re-ran 'aide --check' post-restart confirming baseline persisted and integrity checking still functions cleanly

evidence.requirement: AIDE integrity tool installed and baseline database initialized for /etc coverage on node1
evidence.summary: node1 had no aide package and no enabled yum repos; downloaded compatible RHEL7 rpm from vault.centos.org, installed via rpm, confirmed default aide.conf covers /etc with a tree-wide PERMS rule plus CONTENT_EX/SHA256 rules for critical config files, ran aide --init, and activated the resulting database as aide.db.gz

evidence.requirement: Baseline correctly validates clean state and detects later changes to /etc
evidence.summary: Initial aide --check reported 'All files match AIDE database' (clean). After appending text to the tracked file /etc/issue, aide --check exited 4 and reported 1 changed file with the differing SHA256 hashes, proving detection works. After reverting, aide --check returned to clean, confirming the baseline is intact and usable going forward

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: healthy pre-restart baseline captured
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 325732f1-bc39-4512-b05e-397f42060246, uptime start 2026-09-29 10:24:12, aide.db.gz md5sum be6e20e2..., and a clean aide --check result immediately before restart

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: acknowledged restart and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Issued 'shutdown -r now' in the background so the exec call acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent polls timed out (node down) then succeeded with a new boot_id 0149bfc8-b11a-4d5b-82e3-e834ebf7c1c9 and new uptime start 10:31:17, proving an actual reboot occurred (not just a service restart)

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart: post-restart recovery of integrity baseline verified
evidence.summary: After restart, aide.db.gz md5sum matched the pre-restart value exactly and aide --check again reported 'All files match AIDE database', confirming the /etc integrity baseline survived the restart and remains fully functional
